I couldn't find a specific period for keeping the Tessa dishwasher's original packaging. The Tessa passages advise keeping the packaging if you still have it, because its shaped supports, protective wrapping and outer carton protect the appliance in transport [P2]. Neither passage gives a time limit [P1][P2].

The Tessa guidance does say:
- You don't need the original packaging to request a return. If it's unavailable or unsuitable, you can use sturdy replacement packaging [P2].
- If you no longer have the original packaging, tell customer care so they can discuss suitable protection for transport [P1].
- Missing original packaging doesn't remove your statutory rights [P1].

The retention periods in the other passages apply to different appliances, not the Tessa dishwasher: 51 days for the Ashby tumble dryer [P3], 8 days for the Fenwick cooker hood [P4] and 18 days for the Vale fridge freezer [P5].

I couldn't find the cooking capacity of a Halvard air fryer in the passages provided. They don't mention an air fryer at all. They cover only these Halvard Home products:

- **Corra induction hob:** safe use, cleaning and maintenance [P1]
- **Fenwick cooker hood:** its warranty [P2], energy-saving settings [P3], factory reset [P4] and grease filter cleaning [P5]

I couldn't find a recommended cooling or waiting time before cleaning the Vale fridge freezer in these passages.

The passages do say what to do before cleaning:

- **Cleaning the filter:** Switch off the fridge freezer at the socket and unplug it. Keep the doors closed while you work to help food stay cold [P1].
- **Cleaning the interior for a long absence:** Switch it off and unplug it. Remove all food and let any ice thaw before wiping the interior [P2].

The only related waiting times are not about cleaning:
- After moving the appliance, leave it upright for at least 24 hours before plugging it in [P5].
- Let it cool fully before putting food back in [P5].
- When returning to a holiday home, let it reach its set temperatures before adding chilled or frozen food [P2].

I could not find the answer in the passages provided. They only cover the Halvard Home Ashby tumble dryer: its safe use, resetting, firmware updates, child lock fault and installation [P1][P2][P3][P4][P5]. None of them mention a Halvard hair dryer or its heat and speed settings.

Postcode area LL is in the **Wales and West** service region [P2]. In that region, parts for warranty repairs arrive **within 57 working days** [P1].

Some related points about the repair process:
- An engineer visit is offered within 46 hours of your claim being accepted. This is a commitment to offer a visit, not to complete the repair during it [P1].
- If a part is needed, the engineer may not be able to finish the work until the part is available and a return visit has been arranged. Halvard Home will explain how the part's arrival affects the repair [P1].
- Living in an LL postcode does not automatically make your address eligible for an engineer visit. Customer service will check your location and confirm whether an engineer can attend [P2].

I couldn't find anything in the passages about a wall bracket or batch 4867 for the Brio kettle. They don't mention wall brackets or batch-specific recalls at all.

The closest relevant guidance is general recall advice. If you receive a recall notice affecting your Brio kettle, stop using it and follow the advice from Halvard Home [P2]. Don't pass it on to someone else while its safety is in doubt, and contact customer support if you need help interpreting the notice [P2]. Keep the kettle's identification details available so customer support can check whether it is covered [P3].

To find out whether batch 4867 is affected and what to do, contact Halvard Home customer support directly.

**The passages don't say which region the NG postcode area belongs to,** so I can't confirm your timeframe from them alone.

NG is generally the Nottingham postcode area, which would put you in the Midlands, but that is outside knowledge rather than something the passages state. If you are in the Midlands, recall collections are made within **21 working days** [P3]. You will not be asked to transport an unsafe appliance yourself or arrange disposal as a condition of getting recall support [P3].

Recall collection timeframes for the other regions are:
- North of England: 33 working days [P1]
- Wales and West: 39 working days [P2]
- London and South East: 53 working days [P4]
- Scotland North: 51 working days [P5]

To confirm which region applies to you, check with Halvard Home's customer support.

I couldn't find any information in the passages about wall brackets or batch 9503 for the Mira robot vacuum. None of the passages mention wall brackets or batch numbers.

The closest relevant guidance is general: if a safety notice or recall applies to your Mira robot vacuum, follow that notice and don't reinstall or restart the vacuum against its instructions [P4]. For advice, you can contact Halvard Home rather than modifying the robot, charging base or power supply [P4].

Let the Ashby tumble dryer cool for **111 minutes** before cleaning it. Before that, switch it off and disconnect it from the electricity supply [P1].

There is one exception. If you are descaling the KX-3673 filter inside the water collection tank, the descaling instructions say to switch off and unplug the dryer and leave it to cool for **30 minutes** [P5].

The filter-cleaning and warning-light guides only say to let the dryer cool, without giving a time [P2][P4]. For general cleaning, the 111-minute figure in the safety guidance is the one that applies.

Let the Brio kettle cool for **36 minutes** before cleaning it [P1]. First, switch it off and unplug it [P1].

Even after 36 minutes, treat surfaces with care if they still feel hot [P1]. The filter-cleaning and descaling instructions also say to let the kettle cool completely before you start [P2][P3].

The other waiting times in the passages are for different situations, not routine cleaning:
- **At least 30 minutes** before checking the kettle after a burning smell [P4]
- **At least 15 minutes** before checking it after a flashing warning light [P5]

After moving the Mira robot vacuum, **wait 37 hours before switching it on** [P5].

During that wait:
- Leave it switched off, and make sure it can't be started by accident through its controls or the app [P5].
- Check its condition and the new installation area before you reconnect the charging base. Don't switch it on if you suspect damage [P5].

Before you start it again:
- Make sure the charging contacts are dry and free of visible dirt, and that the base sits securely [P5].
- Review the robot's saved map and restricted areas. Settings from its old position may not protect stairs, cables or other hazards in the new location [P5].

I couldn't find how long repairs to the Tessa dishwasher are covered for. The passages cover safe use, troubleshooting and descaling for the Tessa dishwasher, but none of them give a repair guarantee or warranty period.

The closest they come is advising you to contact Halvard Home if you suspect a safety fault or need help [P1], and to contact Halvard Home support for an inspection when problems persist [P2][P3][P4][P5]. Halvard Home is probably the best source for the repair coverage period.

On the Ashby tumble dryer, E-2194 means a factory reset was interrupted before the saved settings could be cleared, so your previous preferences may still be active [P1].

To try the reset again [P1]:
1. Switch the dryer off, unplug it and wait five minutes.
2. Check that the drum is empty, then close the door.
3. Plug the dryer back in and switch it on without selecting a programme.
4. Press and hold the Temperature and Delay Start buttons together for ten seconds.
5. Release both buttons when the display shows "Reset", then wait until the programme selection screen returns.

A completed reset clears saved drying preferences and delayed starts. If the warning comes back, stop repeating the reset and contact Halvard Home support [P1].

I'm assuming your smart water boiler is the **Brio kettle**, since that's the only appliance these passages describe.

The Brio kettle connects to a **2.4 GHz** home Wi-Fi network. If your router offers separate networks, choose the 2.4 GHz option rather than 5 GHz [P1]. The voice assistant pairing steps also say to connect your phone to your home's 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network before reconnecting the kettle [P2].

KX-9283 is the part number for the **Wi-Fi module in the Ashby tumble dryer**. This module connects the dryer to the Halvard Home app [P1].

If this module gets stuck in standby, the dryer can't broadcast its setup signal, so it won't appear in the app [P1]. To fix this:

- Switch the dryer off at the socket for 60 seconds, then back on.
- Connect your phone to your home's 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.
- Hold the dryer's Wi-Fi button for five seconds until its light flashes.
- Select "Add appliance" in the app [P1].

If the dryer still doesn't appear, contact Halvard Home support. Don't open the casing or replace the module yourself [P1].

Don't confuse it with KX-9996, a different part in the same dryer. KX-9996 is the voice connection module [P3].

**Replace the filter every 24 weeks.** This applies where an extraction filter is fitted. [P1]

A few related points:

- Follow the cleaning and fitting instructions supplied with the filter. A clogged or badly fitted filter can reduce extraction performance. [P1]
- Only wash the filter if the user instructions say it is washable. [P1]
- If you do clean it, first switch off the hob and extractor and let them cool. Then wash the filter in warm water with a little washing-up liquid and a soft brush, rinse it, and let it dry completely before refitting. [P2]
- If the filter is damaged or won't fit securely, contact Halvard Home support. [P2]

To get your Tessa dishwasher ready for a long absence:

**Before you leave**
- Run a wash to clear any dirty dishes. When the programme finishes, unload the dishwasher and let the interior cool. [P1]
- Clean the filter as described in your user manual, then wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth. [P1] Let the dishwasher cool for 7 minutes before cleaning it. If the cleaning step requires the power to be off, disconnect the electrical supply first. [P2]

**Shutting it down**
- For an extended absence, switch off the electricity supply and close the dishwasher's water supply valve. [P1]
- Leave the door slightly open, if it's safe to do so, so moisture can escape. [P1] Be aware that an open door can be a trip hazard, and children or pets could climb onto it or reach inside. [P2]

**If the cottage could freeze**
- Ask a qualified installer about draining the appliance before you leave. [P1]

**When you return**
- Restore the electricity and water supplies, and check for leaks before running a wash. [P1] If the dishwasher leaks or behaves unexpectedly, stop using it and contact Halvard Home. [P2]

You have **93 days** to request an exchange of your Keel washing machine for a different colour [P1].

Some conditions apply:
- Exchanges depend on availability and on the condition of the returned appliance [P1].
- Halvard Home will explain any charges before you decide whether to go ahead [P1].

To start the request, contact Halvard Home customer support and explain why you want to return the machine. Provide your name, delivery address and proof of purchase [P1].

Extended Care extends the standard warranty by **58 months**. It covers mechanical and electrical faults that develop after the standard warranty ends [P1]. Your plan confirmation shows the exact dates your extended cover begins and ends [P1].

Don't confuse this with **Extended Care Plus**, a separate plan that extends the standard warranty by 50 months [P2].

Under the general recall terms, a recalled appliance is collected **within 18 working days of your reply** [P1]. Before collection, Halvard Home will agree the arrangements with you and explain how to prepare the appliance safely. You should mention any access difficulties or support needs when you respond [P1].

However, the regional sections give different collection times:

- **Island Areas:** within 44 working days [P2].
- **London and South East:** within 53 working days. This period starts when Halvard Home confirms that collection is required, not when you reply. Working days exclude weekends and bank holidays that apply to the collection address [P3].
- **Wales and West:** within 39 working days [P4].

The passages don't say how the 18-day general commitment relates to these longer regional times. If you tell me which region you live in, I can point you to the timing stated for that area. Your recall notice or Halvard Home's support team can confirm which commitment applies to you [P1].

A reminder goes out **3 weeks before** your Ashby tumble dryer's service is due [P1]. It's sent to the contact details on your account, so let Halvard Home know if those change [P1].

Some useful points:
- The reminder invites you to arrange a visit. It does not mean an appointment has been booked. You book through the details in the reminder or through your customer account [P1].
- If the reminder never reaches you, you should still follow your recorded servicing schedule [P1]. You can check your service due date in your customer account or by asking customer care [P1].

I could not find how long the Tessa dishwasher's built-in test takes. None of the passages mention a built-in test or self-test feature.

The closest information is about engineer visits. A routine service of the Tessa dishwasher takes about 230 minutes [P2], and the engineer may need to run the dishwasher as part of the checks [P2]. That is the length of a full service visit, not of a built-in test.

**A refurbished part fitted to the Keel washing machine is covered for 50 weeks.** [P1] Refurbished parts are sometimes used when new parts are scarce. They are checked for safety, condition and suitability before fitting, and Halvard Home will tell you if one has been used and how to report a problem with it. [P1]

The passages also give a different figure for replacement parts generally: parts fitted during a warranty repair are covered for a further 218 days from the fitting date shown on the repair paperwork. [P2] The 50-week figure applies specifically to refurbished parts. [P1] However, the passages don't explain how the two figures relate when a refurbished part is fitted under warranty.

Two further points apply:
- If the appliance's original cover would protect the part for longer, that protection continues. Fitting a replacement part does not shorten existing cover. [P2]
- Labour is free only for the first 34 months, so labour charges may apply after that even if the part is still covered. [P2]

The Tessa dishwasher's internal diagnostic test runs for 52 minutes [P1]. Engineers must use the approved test procedure and record the outcome in the job notes [P1]. A completed test does not prove the reported fault is fixed. The results should be compared with the original symptoms [P1].

I couldn't find how long the Brio kettle's built-in check takes. None of the passages describes a built-in check or self-test.

The passages give these other timings, which may not be what you mean:
- **Factory reset:** Hold the power button for 10 seconds, until the indicator light flashes twice. [P1]
- **After a flashing warning light or fault message:** Leave the kettle to cool for at least 15 minutes before checking it. [P2][P3]
- **Before cleaning:** Let the kettle cool for 36 minutes. [P5]

The Brio kettle's **internal diagnostic test runs for 19 minutes** [P1].

This test comes from the engineer service manual, so it is not a check you run at home. It must be run only under the approved test procedure, with the required guards and test equipment in place [P1]. Passing the diagnostic test does not replace the electrical safety and functional checks required after a repair [P1].

If you meant a full routine service visit, that takes about 135 minutes, though this is a guide rather than a guarantee [P2].

If your Keel washing machine vibrates more than usual, **pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop** before checking anything [P1]. Then work through these checks:

1. **Rebalance the load.** An uneven load can cause vibration during the spin cycle. Once the door unlocks, spread heavy items such as towels evenly around the drum, then restart the programme [P1]. Never force the door open [P1][P4]. While the door is open, also check for coins, keys or other loose objects [P4].

2. **Make sure the machine is level and stable.** It should stand firmly on a hard, level floor with all four feet touching the floor. It shouldn't rock when you gently push opposite corners [P1]. If it does rock, switch it off and unplug it before adjusting the feet [P4].

3. **Check the transit bolts if the machine is newly installed.** Use the installation guide to confirm the transit bolts were removed [P1]. These bolts protect the drum during delivery but must be removed before use [P5]. If any are still in place:
   - Switch off and unplug the machine.
   - Remove all the bolts from the rear, following the installation guide.
   - Fit the supplied plastic caps into the empty holes.
   - Keep the bolts for any future move [P5].

4. **Know when to stop and get help.**
   - If strong vibration continues, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support [P1].
   - If you notice severe shaking, smoke or a burning smell, switch the machine off and disconnect it from the electricity supply if it's safe to do so [P2].
   - Also stop and contact support if you hear grinding or see leaking water [P4].
   - If there is a fire or an immediate threat to safety, move away and contact the emergency services [P2].

Don't attempt repairs yourself or keep using a damaged appliance. Contact Halvard Home through its official support channels instead [P2].

**Warranty engineer visit:** In the North of England, Halvard Home offers a warranty engineer visit within 92 hours of accepting your claim [P1]. That appointment is for an engineer to attend and assess or carry out the repair, not a promise that the repair will be finished at that visit [P1]. If parts are needed, they arrive within 36 working days, and fitting is arranged separately [P1].

**Recall notification:** I could not find this. None of the passages say how soon Halvard Home will tell you about a recall after it is issued. The closest related commitment is that recall collections in the North of England happen within 33 working days. That period starts when Halvard Home confirms your item needs collecting under a recall, not when the recall is issued [P2].

In Wales and West, a warranty engineer visit is offered within 46 hours of your claim being accepted [P1]. This is a commitment to offer a visit. It doesn't guarantee the repair will be finished on that visit [P1]. If a part is needed, it can take up to 57 working days to arrive, and the engineer may need to come back once it does [P1].

A routine service for the Brio kettle costs £78.00 [P2]. That price covers the engineer's routine inspection, the standard service checks and an assessment of the kettle's condition. Repairs, replacement parts and work outside the routine service are not included unless confirmed when you book [P2].

Let the Tessa dishwasher cool for 7 minutes before cleaning it [P1]. If any surfaces are still hot after that, wait until they are safe to touch [P1].

Before cleaning:
- **Power:** Unplug it before any cleaning the instructions say must be done without power. Never spray water onto electrical parts or use a steam cleaner [P1].
- **Filter:** To clean the filter, switch off and unplug the dishwasher, then let it cool before removing the filter [P2].

Stop the machine, make it safe, check a few external causes, and then contact Halvard Home support.

**1. Stop and make it safe**
- Stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap [P1][P3], if you can reach it safely [P5].
- Switch off and unplug the machine only if the plug and the area around it are dry [P1][P2][P3]. Never touch a wet socket or plug [P1][P4], and don't reach through standing water to unplug it [P5].
- If water may have reached the electrical supply, get help from a qualified electrician [P5].

**2. Check the likely causes without moving the machine**
Once it's safe, wipe up the water and check:
- the visible inlet hose connections, for drips [P1]
- the drain hose, in case it has slipped out of its drain [P1]
- the detergent drawer, for water running down from it. Too much detergent can cause excess foam and leaks [P1]

**3. Don't run another cycle or attempt repairs**
- Don't use the machine again until the cause of the leak is known [P1][P5].
- Don't remove panels or try to seal the leak yourself [P3][P4].

**4. Contact Halvard Home support**
- Contact support if the hoses look secure or the water is coming from beneath the casing [P1].
- Have ready your purchase details, serial number, address and preferred appointment dates, plus a description of where the water appears [P2][P3]. Also mention any visible damage or recent changes to the plumbing or electrical connection [P4].
- A leak under the machine can come from a cracked drain pump housing [P3]. Leaks can also come from a damaged door seal, a loose connection or another internal component, and an engineer will find the source [P4]. The passages give conflicting part numbers for the drain pump: KX-2446 in [P2] and KX-3928 in [P3]. Check with support which one applies before quoting it.

**Costs and warranty**
- The machine has a two-year warranty from delivery. If a manufacturing defect makes the pump housing crack and leak within that time, the pump is repaired or replaced free of charge [P2].
- Arrange a warranty assessment before attempting any repair yourself [P2].
- A diagnosis costs £38.00 if no repair follows. Your warranty and statutory rights are unaffected [P4].

You should **wait 45 hours** after moving your Lumen smart thermostat before switching it on [P1].

The waiting period doesn't replace a safe installation or a damage check [P1]. Before switching it on:

- **Check for damage.** Inspect the device at the new location before arranging installation. If it has been dropped, crushed or exposed to water, don't connect it to the electrical supply; contact Halvard Home instead [P1].
- **Check the backplate.** A cracked retaining clip can stop the thermostat sitting securely. If a clip is cracked, have the backplate (KX-6505) replaced before restoring power, and don't tape the thermostat in place [P2].
- **Leave it disconnected if you have concerns.** If you're worried about its condition, keep it off even after the 45 hours have passed [P1].
- **Use a qualified installer for wiring.** Any work involving fixed wiring or connections to your heating system should be done by a qualified installer [P1][P2].
